title: Don’t Sleep on This Hatch Sleep Clock Deal
gist: Wired promotes the first sale on the Hatch Sleep Clock: 25% off, $250 down to $188, on November 19-20. The device combines a sunrise alarm, light, sound machine and contactless motion-based sleep tracking with no subscription needed for sleep data. Against an Oura Ring 5 and Apple Watch Series 12 it matched on sleep duration but not on sleep stages.

insights.claim: The Hatch Sleep Clock got its first-ever discount for Black Friday: 25 percent off at Hatch and Amazon on November 19-20, down to $188 from $250. That is just $18 more than the $170 retail price of the older Hatch Restore 3.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: A first discount soon after launch narrows the price gap to the previous generation, which could push buyers toward the newer model.

insights.claim: Hatch is also discounting the Restore 3 to $130 ($40 off) and Hatch Baby to $66 ($14 off).
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Discounting across Hatch's whole lineup is a holiday promotional signal.

insights.claim: The Hatch Sleep Clock uses a built-in motion sensor to track movement and breathing without contact, adding passive sleep monitoring that the Hatch Restore 3 lacked. It appeals to people who dislike wearing devices to bed.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Contactless bedside sensing is a competitor to wearable sleep trackers for people who don't want to wear a device.

insights.claim: Compared with an Oura Ring 5 and Apple Watch Series 12, the Hatch Sleep Clock gave broadly matching sleep-duration estimates but less consistent sleep-stage readings. It does not measure heart rate or detect snoring, and its accuracy depends on placement.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Wearables like Oura and Apple Watch keep their lead in health-grade metrics, so contactless clocks are complements rather than replacements.

insights.claim: Wired's reviewer does not recommend replacing a dedicated wearable with the Hatch Sleep Clock if detailed health tracking is the priority. She calls it the best all-in-one bedside device.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Hatch is positioned as a bedside device that bundles features, not a health tracker, which limits its overlap with Oura and Apple Watch.

insights.claim: Unlike most sleep trackers, Hatch does not require a subscription to see sleep data. Its Hatch+ membership ($6 per month) only unlocks the full audio library.
insights.speaker: Boutayna Chokrane
insights.so_what: Hatch puts its paywall on content rather than data, a different subscription strategy from competitors that charge for access to sleep data.
